title: Conormal basis of a Koszul-regular sequence
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $r\geq0$, $f:\{1,\ldots,r\}\to A$ a Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence], and $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$. For $B=A/I$, the conormal classes $f_i\bmod I^2$ form a $B$-basis of $I/I^2$ [def-sc-koszul-conormal-comparison]. The Koszul complex is as in [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex].

source.place: Tags 0CEM and 062I, lemma-koszul-regular-H1-regular and lemma-H1-regular-quasi-regular, first paragraph of the proof

proof.text: Koszul-regularity implies H_1(K)=0. The degree-one map E=A^r to I is surjective, and its kernel is the image of the second Koszul differential. This gives the exact sequence exterior^2 E -> E -> I -> 0.

Tensor this right-exact sequence with B=A/I. The second Koszul differential has entries in I, so its reduction is zero. Consequently B tensor E maps isomorphically onto B tensor I = I/I^2. The images of the standard basis vectors are precisely the generating conormal classes. Transport the standard basis along this isomorphism. This is the first paragraph of Stacks 062I, not the subsequent higher-degree quasi-regularity induction.
